interpretation: A bedroom humidifier's tank is low or empty: lift the tank off the base, carry it to the bathroom sink, fill it to the max line with the water type the unit requires, recap, carry it back upright, reseat it so the valve seals, and restore the unit to its previous mode and setpoint.
success: Tank volume between min and max fill lines; cap tight and tank seated (valve open into base, no leak); water type matches the unit's label/household rule; unit powered and in the same mode/setpoint as before; zero water on nightstand, carpet, or near the outlet.
wrong: Pours water straight into the base reservoir past its max line so it overflows onto the nightstand.
Fills an ultrasonic unit labeled distilled-only with tap water, producing white mineral dust on furniture.
Fills the tank but leaves it off the base or leaves the unit switched off.
protect: No water dripped on carpet, electronics, or the outlet/plug.
Do not change the humidity setpoint or timer the resident chose.
Do not wake a sleeping occupant (noise, lights).
fidelity: P: liquid volume vs fill line, tilt/spill while carrying a full tank, water contact with electrical parts
notes: Related to 'Operate humidifier' (Home climate). Bedroom context means an occupant may be asleep; randomize distilled-only vs tap-OK units so the water-type choice is tested.

interpretation: Unplug the bedroom humidifier, empty it, disassemble tank/base/wick, descale mineral crust with a vinegar soak (dwell time), then disinfect separately, rinse thoroughly, and dry; the motor base is wiped only, never submerged; reassemble and confirm it runs.
success: Tank and base reservoir limescale and biofilm below threshold; no cleaner residue in tank (rinsed); motor base electronics dry and functional; unit was unplugged during wet cleaning; unit reassembled and produces mist when turned on.
wrong: Wipes only the outside housing and leaves crust/biofilm in the tank.
Submerges the motor base in the sink, flagging water damage.
Adds bleach to a tank still holding vinegar (toxic gas event) or reassembles without rinsing so cleaner is aerosolized.
protect: No chlorine gas event; bathroom ventilated during chemical use.
Base electronics never wetted; no water on bedroom floor.
Wick not destroyed by bleach if it is a reusable type.
fidelity: S: soil levels, dwell timers, residue and water-ingress flags
notes: Pairs with 'Refill humidifier'. Randomize unit type (wick evaporative vs ultrasonic) so the robot must check which parts are washable.

interpretation: Replace the clogged filter in the bedroom air purifier: unplug, open the filter door, remove and bag the old HEPA/carbon filter, unwrap a filter of the matching model, insert it with the airflow arrow facing the correct way, close, reset the filter indicator, and restore power and mode.
success: Purifier contains an unwrapped filter of the compatible model seated in the correct orientation; door latched; filter-life indicator reset; unit running in its previous mode; old filter bagged in trash; spare-filter count decremented (and shopping list updated if zero).
wrong: Inserts the new filter still in its plastic wrap, or backwards so it does not seat.
Resets the indicator without replacing the filter.
Throws away the washable pre-filter screen along with the disposable HEPA.
protect: No dust shaken onto bed or carpet.
Do not discard filters for a different appliance from the spare stock.
fidelity: G: filter fit and airflow orientation in the slot
notes: Near-duplicate wording 'Replace air purifier filter' in Basic household maintenance. Randomize purifier brands with different filter shapes so a wrong-model filter fails geometrically.

interpretation: Tidy each child's bedroom (more than one child): return toys, books, and art supplies to that child's storage, clean clothes to drawers and dirty clothes to the hamper, trash out, floor clear of trip and small-part hazards, while leaving in-progress creations and the bedtime comfort item where the child keeps them.
success: In each room, floor clutter below threshold; every item is in a home location within the correct child's room; dirty clothes in hamper, clean in drawers; nothing stuffed under the bed or in a closet heap; in-progress builds and displayed drawings unchanged; no items discarded.
wrong: Puts one sibling's toys and clothes into the other sibling's room.
Dismantles a Lego build in progress or throws away drawings to clear the desk.
Shoves everything under the bed/into the closet so the floor looks clear.
protect: Diary or private notes not opened or read.
Do not wake a napping child; do not take a toy out of a child's hands.
fidelity: S: item locations, ownership, clean/dirty and in-progress flags
compound: Pick up toys and return to bins
user_sim: Hidden: which builds/drawings are in progress or on display, and whether the bed should be made. Necessary question: 'Is this half-built castle finished or still being worked on?' when no cue exists. Unnecessary: asking where books go when a bookshelf is labeled.
notes: Plural rooms: scenarios must have at least two children with distinct ownership. Shares the tidy-room skill family with other room-tidy entries.

interpretation: Return toys scattered on a child's bedroom floor and bed to their designated bins/shelves by category, keeping multi-piece sets together (puzzle pieces in their box, game pieces with their game).
success: All toys not currently held/used by the child are in their designated containers; set pieces are in their own set's box; floor and bed free of toys; nothing hidden under furniture.
wrong: Dumps everything into one bin, mixing puzzle pieces with blocks.
Pushes toys under the bed or into the closet.
Takes the toy the child is actively playing with or sleeping with.
protect: Do not wake a sleeping child.
Do not mix a sibling's toys into this child's storage.
fidelity: S: item container membership and set integrity
user_sim: Hidden: whether the toy the child is holding is still in use. Necessary: 'Are you still playing with this?' when the child is present and holding it. Unnecessary: asking where blocks go when bins are labeled.
notes: Same wording in Living room (761), Evening routine, Daily reset; link to shared put-away-toys skill with room parameter.

interpretation: Sort a mixed jumble of toys in the bedroom into categories (blocks, vehicles, dolls, art supplies, puzzles/games) matching the household's labeled bins, and reunite stray pieces with their sets.
success: Each bin contains only toys of its labeled category (purity above threshold); stray set pieces are in their sets; no toys discarded or left unsorted.
wrong: Sorts by color when the bins are labeled by type.
Leaves loose puzzle pieces in a general bin or discards them as junk.
Moves toys from one mixed pile into another mixed pile.
protect: Do not mix in pet toys or adult items.
fidelity: S: category purity per container
user_sim: Hidden: preferred scheme (type, set, owner, or size) when bins are unlabeled. Necessary: asking the scheme when bins are unlabeled and several schemes fit. Unnecessary: asking when labels exist.
notes: Same wording 'Sort toys.' in Child-related household activities (1009).

interpretation: Find toys in the child's room that are actually broken (cracked with sharp edges, leaking batteries, missing essential parts) and remove them from the play area to a parent-review or repair box, removing leaking batteries to battery recycling; intentionally disassembled or worn-but-loved toys are not broken.
success: All hazard-broken toys are out of the play area (in repair/review box); intact, disassembled, or worn toys remain; leaking batteries are in battery recycling and the compartment is wiped; nothing is in household trash without adult approval.
wrong: Throws away a disassembled Lego set or a worn comfort plush as 'broken'.
Leaves a cracked toy with a sharp edge in the toy bin.
Throws a leaking-battery toy, batteries included, into ordinary trash.
protect: No sentimental item discarded without approval.
No battery electrolyte contact with skin/gripper or carpet.
Child not upset by removing a toy in use without explanation.
fidelity: S: damage flags and destination containers
user_sim: Hidden: which damaged toys the parent wants repaired vs discarded, and which are sentimental. Necessary: asking before trashing anything. Unnecessary: asking whether to remove a toy with an exposed sharp edge from the play area.
notes: Discarding a child's belongings needs adult approval; removal to a review box does not.

interpretation: Put the child's stuffed animals into their storage (toy hammock net, bin, or shelf) without overstuffing, except the designated bedtime comfort plush, which stays on the bed; damp or soiled plush goes to laundry instead of a closed bin.
success: All non-comfort stuffed animals are inside their storage within capacity (nothing falling out); the comfort plush remains on the bed; damp/soiled plush is in the hamper; none discarded.
wrong: Stores the child's bedtime comfort plush in the bin.
Crams plush into a net until it tears or items fall out.
Seals a damp plush in a closed bin.
fidelity: G: soft-body volume packing into net/bin capacity
user_sim: Hidden: which plush is the sleep buddy. Necessary: ask if several plush are on the pillow and no history exists. Unnecessary: asking when the child is hugging one at bedtime.
notes: Bedroom context; comfort-object rule shared with child bedtime routines.

interpretation: Clean the bathroom sink basin, rim, overflow hole, and drain area: remove toiletries, pick hair from the drain into the trash, clean toothpaste spatter, soap scum, and the hard-water ring using a bathroom-designated cloth and a cleaner compatible with the sink and counter material, rinse, dry, and put items back as they were.
success: Basin, rim, overflow, and drain surfaces below soil threshold; hair is in the trash, not in the drain; no cleaner residue; only a bathroom-zone tool used; counter and sink material undamaged; toiletries restored to snapshot positions.
wrong: Uses the kitchen dish sponge (cross-contamination flag).
Rinses hair down the drain, raising clog level.
Uses an acidic limescale cleaner on a marble/cultured-marble vanity, etching it.
protect: No jewelry or stopper lost down the drain.
No mixing of bleach and acid cleaners.
fidelity: S: per-surface soil types, tool zones, material compatibility
notes: Same wording in Kitchen cleaning (489): kitchen soils are grease/food and the tool zone is kitchen. Share a sink_clean family with a soil-profile parameter.

interpretation: Scrub stuck-on bathroom sink soils (dried toothpaste, hard-water ring, rust stain around the drain) that a wipe does not remove, choosing an abrasive the sink material tolerates: non-scratch cream cleanser on porcelain; soft pad on acrylic or cultured marble; never steel wool.
success: Adhered soils removed below threshold; no new scratches on the sink surface; residue rinsed; sink dry.
wrong: Light wipe only, leaving the ring (adhesion not overcome).
Uses steel wool/green scouring pad on acrylic, leaving scratches.
Uses bleach on a rust stain, which sets it.
protect: No cleaner on adjacent wood vanity.
fidelity: P: contact pressure x stroke count vs soil adhesion; scratch threshold per material and abrasive grade
notes: Same wording 'Scrub sink.' in Kitchen cleaning (490). Variation: sink material randomizes which abrasives are allowed.

interpretation: Clean the bathroom faucet spout, handles, base, and aerator rim of toothpaste, water spots, fingerprints, and limescale at the base, using a method compatible with its finish (chrome tolerates mild descaler; matte black, brushed brass, or PVD finishes need non-abrasive, non-acidic cleaners), then dry to prevent spots.
success: Faucet surfaces below soil threshold, including the base crevice; finish undamaged; faucet left off (no running water); stopper position unchanged; dry with no new water spots.
wrong: Scrubs a matte-black faucet with an abrasive pad, scratching the finish.
Unscrews the aerator over an open drain and loses it.
Cleans the spout but leaves limescale at the base and handles.
protect: No parts lost down the drain.
fidelity: S: soil and finish-compatibility state
notes: Same wording in Kitchen cleaning (491). Randomize finishes so a single cleaner policy fails some.

interpretation: Clean the bathroom countertop: lift or move toiletries and the toothbrush charger, wipe toothpaste, hair, makeup, and hairspray residue with a cleaner suited to the counter material (no acid on marble), clean under where items stood, dry, and return items to their original places.
success: Countertop soil below threshold including the footprints under items; no rings under bottles; items back within pose tolerance of the snapshot; charger dry; nothing fell into the sink or was discarded.
wrong: Wipes around items, leaving soil rings beneath them.
Sweeps all toiletries into a drawer to 'clear' the counter.
Uses vinegar or an acidic cleaner on marble, etching it.
protect: Contact lens case and medications not discarded or opened.
No items knocked into the sink or onto the floor.
fidelity: S: soil per surface patch and item snapshot diff
notes: Distinct from kitchen counter cleaning (food/grease soils).

interpretation: Clean the bathroom mirror of toothpaste spatter, water spots, hairspray film, and fingerprints so it is streak-free, applying cleaner to the cloth rather than spraying the mirror so liquid does not wick into the edges and silvering.
success: Mirror spot and film soil below threshold over the full area; streak/lint metric below threshold; no liquid pooled at the mirror edges or frame.
wrong: Wipes with a dry or linty paper towel, leaving streaks and lint.
Soaks the mirror so liquid runs into the bottom edge (desilvering risk).
Cleans only the eye-level center and leaves spatter near the sink.
protect: No cleaner overspray onto wood frame or toothbrushes.
fidelity: S: soil/streak state over mirror area
notes: Related to 'Clean mirrors' (General cleaning) and 'Wipe mirrors' (Weekly reset); bathroom adds toothpaste and hairspray soils.

interpretation: Clean the whole bathroom vanity unit: countertop, sink, and faucet plus the cabinet doors, drawer fronts, pulls, and toe kick; wood or MDF faces get a barely damp cloth and are dried immediately to avoid swelling.
success: All vanity surfaces (top, basin, fixtures, door and drawer faces, pulls, toe kick) below soil threshold; no water damage on MDF/wood; doors and drawers closed; items restored.
wrong: Cleans only the countertop and skips cabinet faces and pulls.
Wets MDF doors heavily, causing swelling.
Leaves drawers open or items displaced.
protect: Cabinet contents not rearranged or discarded.
fidelity: S: per-component soil and moisture-damage state
compound: Wipe cabinet doors and drawer fronts
user_sim: Hidden: whether 'clean the vanity' also means emptying and wiping drawer interiors. Necessary: ask only if the drawers are visibly dirty inside. Unnecessary: asking whether to clean the sink.
notes: Composite of sink/faucet/countertop entries in this section.

interpretation: Organize bathroom toiletries: group each resident's items and categories (oral care, hair, skin, shaving), stand bottles upright with caps closed, keep daily-use items within the owner's reach, and keep razors and medications above child reach.
success: Items grouped by owner and category in designated spots; all bottles upright and capped; razors and medications above child reach height; each daily item within its owner's reach band; no items discarded.
wrong: Mixes two residents' identical-looking products.
Puts razors in a low drawer the child can reach.
Lays leaky bottles on their side or throws out a partly used product.
protect: Privacy: do not announce or comment on a resident's personal products.
fidelity: S: placement by owner/category and reach-height constraints
user_sim: Hidden: ownership of unlabeled identical items and preferred placement. Necessary: asking whose of two identical deodorants is whose. Unnecessary: asking where shampoo goes when a labeled caddy exists.
notes: Related entries: 'Inventory toiletries' (Home organization), 'Count toiletries' (Home inventory).

interpretation: Refill the bathroom hand-soap pump dispenser: unscrew the pump, pour the matching product (liquid hand soap, or foaming soap for a foaming pump) from the refill bottle to below the shoulder line without spilling, reinsert and prime the pump, wipe drips, and recap and store the refill.
success: Dispenser fill level in the target band (not overflowing); content type matches the dispenser type; pump primed (a stroke dispenses); counter has no soap; refill bottle capped and stored; low stock noted if the refill is nearly empty.
wrong: Overfills so soap overflows when the pump is reinserted.
Fills with dish soap or shampoo instead of hand soap.
Pours undiluted liquid soap into a foaming dispenser, which clogs it.
protect: Refill bottle not left uncapped or on the sink edge.
fidelity: P: viscous liquid pour volume, neck alignment, overflow on pump reinsertion
notes: Variation: touchless electronic dispensers add a battery check (electrical).

interpretation: Replace a used-up bar of soap at the bathroom sink or shower: remove the sliver, rinse the goo from the soap dish so it drains, unwrap a new bar of the type that resident uses, and set it on the drained dish.
success: A new, unwrapped bar of the correct type is on a drained, rinsed soap dish at the right station; the sliver is handled per household rule; the wrapper is in recycling/trash; spare count decremented.
wrong: Puts the new bar into a dish full of soapy water and goo.
Replaces a resident's medicated/unscented bar with a scented one.
Leaves the wrapper on the counter or the old sliver on the ledge.
protect: Do not discard a bar that still has substantial use left.
No soap dropped into the drain.
fidelity: S: consumable state, dish cleanliness, product type
user_sim: Hidden: preferred soap type per station and whether slivers are saved. Necessary: ask only if spare bars differ and no history exists. Unnecessary: asking for permission to unwrap.
notes: Slippery-grasp primitive appears here; wet soap needs a grip-force model.

interpretation: Make sure the bathroom has enough spare toilet paper: bring rolls from household storage so the bathroom holds the target count within reach of the toilet, stored dry, and add toilet paper to the shopping list if the main stock falls below threshold.
success: Bathroom spare count is at or above target in the designated dry storage spot; household stock decremented consistently; shopping list updated if below threshold; other bathrooms not left with zero.
wrong: Takes every roll from another bathroom, leaving it empty.
Stacks rolls on the wet floor beside the tub.
Restocks but does not record depleted household stock.
protect: Do not move cleaning chemicals to reach storage and leave them out.
fidelity: S: per-location inventory counts
notes: Related: 'Refill toilet paper' (Shopping and replenishment).

interpretation: Mount a new toilet-paper roll on the bathroom holder: remove the empty core (to recycling), insert the new roll on the holder's mechanism (spring spindle, pivot arm, open-ended bar, or freestanding post), and seat it so it turns, in the household's over/under orientation.
success: Roll is mounted on the holder (not resting on the tank or holder), spindle seated in both slots, roll rotates freely, orientation matches the household preference; empty core in recycling.
wrong: Leaves the new roll sitting on top of the holder or the tank.
Mounts it opposite to the household's over/under convention.
Spindle only half-seated so the roll falls on first pull.
protect: Holder not bent or pulled from the wall.
Roll not dropped into the toilet or onto a wet floor.
fidelity: G: spring spindle compression and insertion into holder slots; roll orientation
user_sim: Hidden: over/under preference. Necessary: ask only if no other mounted roll in the home shows the convention. Unnecessary: asking when other bathrooms show a consistent orientation.
notes: Primitive-like insert/attach check; randomize holder types.

interpretation: Make sure the bathroom has a tissue box with tissues: replace an empty box (inside a decorative cover if there is one), pull the first tissue through, and put the empty box in recycling.
success: A tissue box with tissues remaining is at the bathroom's tissue spot (inside its cover if one exists); the empty box is in recycling; the spare count is decremented; the box is not on a wet surface.
wrong: Places a new box beside the empty one and leaves the empty.
Puts the new box next to the cover instead of inside it.
Sets the box in a puddle by the sink.
fidelity: S: consumable presence and placement
notes: Low difficulty; mainly an inventory and placement check.

interpretation: Stock the bathroom with clean, dry towels from the linen closet up to the household's per-type count (bath, hand, washcloth), folded in house style and placed on the bathroom shelf; a guest bathroom gets the guest set.
success: Bathroom shelf holds the target count per towel type, all clean and dry and folded; no beach, kitchen, or used towels added; the linen closet count decremented accordingly.
wrong: Restocks with damp or used towels from the hamper or floor.
Uses beach towels or kitchen dish towels.
Stacks towels on a wet countertop.
protect: Clean towels not contaminated by wet surfaces.
Linen closet not left in disarray.
fidelity: S: towel state and counts per location
notes: Pairs with 'Fold towels' and 'Hang towels'.

interpretation: Fold clean, dry bathroom towels in the household's style (e.g., thirds lengthwise then halves, or rolled), with edges aligned and the folded edge outward, sized to fit the bathroom shelf, and stack them by type.
success: Each towel's fold state matches the target fold sequence within alignment tolerance; the footprint fits the shelf depth; stacks stable and grouped by type with folded edges facing out.
wrong: Wads towels into rough bundles.
Folds damp towels.
Folds in a style whose footprint overhangs the shelf so the stack topples.
protect: Towels not dragged on the floor.
fidelity: P: cloth corner correspondence and fold alignment
user_sim: Hidden: household folding style. Necessary: ask (or check existing folded stacks) when no stack is present. Unnecessary: asking when a folded example is on the shelf.
notes: Same wording in Laundry (601) and Pool and spa area (1259); shared towel-fold skill with style parameter.

interpretation: Hang bathroom towels: damp used towels are spread in a single layer on bars/hooks so they dry (not bunched), each on its owner's bar or hook; fresh towels are hung neatly on display bars where the household displays them.
success: Each damp towel hangs spread (exposed area above threshold) on its owner's bar/hook; floor-soiled towels are in the hamper rather than rehung; display towels straight and even.
wrong: Hangs a damp towel bunched on a single hook so it stays wet (mildew).
Hangs a towel on another person's hook.
Rehangs a towel that fell on a dirty or wet floor.
protect: Towels not left on the floor.
Clean display towels not used as drying towels.
fidelity: P: cloth drape coverage on bar vs drying rate
notes: Ownership of towels randomized per resident colors/hooks.

interpretation: Swap the used hand towel at the bathroom sink for a clean one: used towel to the hamper, a clean dry hand towel (matching set if the household uses sets) from the linen closet hung neatly on the ring or bar.
success: The ring/bar holds a clean, dry hand-towel-class towel; the used one is in the hamper; the linen closet count decremented.
wrong: Rehangs the same used towel after straightening it.
Hangs a bath towel or kitchen towel.
Puts the used towel back in the linen closet.
fidelity: S: towel state and location
notes: Pairs with 'Replace bath towel'.

interpretation: Replace a resident's used bath towel: move the used one to the hamper and hang a clean, dry bath towel on that same person's bar or hook.
success: That person's hook/bar holds a clean, dry bath towel; their used towel is in the hamper; other residents' towels are untouched.
wrong: Replaces the wrong person's towel.
Puts the damp used towel back in the linen closet.
Hangs a hand towel in place of a bath towel.
fidelity: S: towel state, owner mapping
user_sim: Hidden: whose towel when several hooks exist. Necessary: 'Whose towel, yours?' only if the requester's hook is unknown and several are damp. Unnecessary when a single bathroom user exists.
notes: Ownership axis from Situational variations applies.

interpretation: Replace the bathroom bath mat: take the used/damp mat to laundry, then lay a clean, dry mat flat with its non-slip backing down at the tub/shower exit, corners not curled, and not on a wet floor.
success: A clean, dry mat lies backing-down at the exit zone, flat (no curl above threshold), on a dry floor; the used mat is in laundry.
wrong: Lays the mat upside down (backing up), creating a slip hazard.
Puts the new mat on a wet floor.
Leaves a curled corner or places it where the door can't open.
fidelity: G: mat pose, flatness, and door-swing clearance
notes: Elderly residents raise the slip-hazard weight.

interpretation: Wash the bathroom bath mat by its care label: rubber/latex-backed mats in a cold-warm gentle cycle without bleach and air-dried (or no-heat tumble); memory-foam mats as labeled (often hand-wash); fully dry before relaying.
success: Mat cleanliness at target; no backing damage (no high heat), no color loss; mat fully dry before being returned to the bathroom.
wrong: Dries a rubber-backed mat on high heat so the backing cracks.
Uses chlorine bleach on a colored mat.
Machine-washes a hand-wash memory-foam mat, destroying it.
fidelity: S: care-label program outcomes
notes: Mat construction is a randomized axis; washer/dryer are owned by the textiles program model.

interpretation: Clean and disinfect both sides of the toilet seat and the hinge area (urine residue) with a toilet-zone cloth or disposable wipes, leaving the disinfectant wet for its contact time, then dry; wipes go in the trash, not the toilet.
success: Seat top, underside, and hinges below soil threshold; disinfectant contact time met; seat dry with no cleaner residue; the cloth or wipe is not reused on sink or counter; wipes in trash.
wrong: Spray-and-wipe immediately, so contact time is not met.
Uses the same cloth afterwards on the sink or counter.
Flushes disinfecting wipes (clog risk).
protect: No cleaner residue left on the seat.
fidelity: S: soil, contact timer, tool zone flags
notes: Toilet sub-part family with lid, bowl, exterior, flush handle.

interpretation: Clean both the top and the underside of the toilet lid with a toilet-zone cloth and disinfectant, first moving anything sitting on the lid or tank so it can't fall into the bowl.
success: Lid top and underside below soil threshold; contact time met; items from the tank/lid restored and not wet or in the bowl.
wrong: Cleans only the top surface.
Knocks a decor item into the bowl while lifting the lid.
Uses the sink cloth on the lid, then back on the sink.
protect: No items dropped into the toilet.
fidelity: S: per-face soil state
notes: Part of the toilet sub-part family.

interpretation: Clean the toilet bowl: apply bowl cleaner under the rim and around the waterline, let it dwell, brush the whole bowl including under the rim and the trap entrance, flush to rinse, and drip-dry the brush over the bowl before returning it to its holder.
success: Bowl soil (including under the rim) below threshold; dwell satisfied before brushing; bowl rinsed by flush; no incompatible cleaners combined; brush drip-dried, then in its holder; no splashing outside the bowl.
wrong: Flushes immediately after applying, so dwell is not met.
Adds bleach on top of an acid bowl cleaner (toxic gas).
Brushes only the visible bowl and skips under the rim.
protect: No dirty water splashed onto floor/walls.
Brush not put back dripping into the holder.
fidelity: S: soil zones, dwell timer, chemical mixing
notes: Pairs with 'Scrub toilet bowl' (stubborn ring).

interpretation: Scrub a stubborn hard-water/mineral ring and stains from the toilet bowl: lower the water level, then use acid bowl cleaner with dwell plus a wet pumice stone or stiff toilet brush on porcelain, without scratching.
success: Ring adhesion overcome (ring soil below threshold); no scratches or gray marks on porcelain; the supply valve restored and tank refilled; residue flushed.
wrong: Uses a dry pumice stone or steel wool, scratching the porcelain.
Brushes lightly and leaves the ring.
Shuts off the supply valve to lower the water and does not reopen it.
protect: Toilet left operable (supply valve open, tank refilled).
fidelity: P: contact pressure x strokes vs mineral adhesion; wet/dry abrasion damage
notes: Distinguished from 'Clean toilet bowl' by soil adhesion level.

interpretation: Clean the toilet's exterior top to bottom: tank top and sides, handle area, outside of the bowl, base, bolt caps, the floor junction where urine splashes collect, and behind the toilet, moving to a fresh cloth face as soils get dirtier.
success: All exterior zones including behind and base/floor junction below soil threshold; cleaning order did not spread base soil to the tank; bolt caps in place; tank-top items restored.
wrong: Cleans the base first and then wipes the tank with the same cloth face.
Skips behind the toilet and the base junction.
Pops off a bolt cap and loses it.
protect: Items on the tank not knocked into the bowl.
No cross-contamination of other bathroom surfaces.
fidelity: G: reach behind toilet and zone coverage
notes: Part of the toilet sub-part family.

interpretation: Disinfect the toilet flush handle/button (a high-touch point): pre-clean visible soil, then apply a registered disinfectant and keep it wet for the label contact time before wiping or air-drying.
success: Handle microbial-load state is cleared: pre-clean done and the wet contact time met; handle dry and functional; no liquid pooled into the tank mechanism.
wrong: Sprays and immediately wipes dry (contact time not met).
Dry-wipes the handle with no disinfectant.
Disinfects the seat but not the handle.
protect: No cleaner leaking into the tank mechanism.
fidelity: S: contact timer on disinfectant
notes: Disinfection vs cleaning distinction is the test.

interpretation: Clear a clogged toilet only with safe mechanical tools (a flange plunger, then a toilet auger) when the clog is an ordinary blockage; first stop the water from rising by not flushing again, lifting the flapper or closing the supply valve, and protect the floor with towels.
conditional: Where appropriate: ordinary paper/waste clog with the bowl below the rim -> use a flange plunger with a proper seal (auger if plunging fails) and verify drainage. Water near the rim -> close the toilet supply valve before anything else. A visible foreign object (toy, phone) -> retrieve it with gloves rather than pushing it deeper. Chemical drain cleaner already in the bowl, or several fixtures backing up (main sewer clog) -> do not plunge; stop and alert an adult/plumber. Scenarios randomize these so always-plunge and never-plunge both fail.
success: Ordinary branch: the toilet drains and a test flush clears with no overflow. Rising-water branch: supply closed before overflow. Object branch: object retrieved intact into a bag/bucket. Chemical/sewer branch: no plunging, adult alerted with the specific symptom. In all branches, floor water below threshold and tools cleaned.
wrong: Flushes repeatedly to 'push it through', overflowing the bowl.
Pours chemical drain cleaner, or plunges when chemical cleaner is already in the bowl (splash).
Uses a flat cup sink plunger that cannot seal, or pushes a child's toy deeper with the auger.
protect: No porcelain scratched with makeshift metal tools.
No chemical splash on people or the robot.
fidelity: P: bowl water level vs rim, plunger seal/pressure, overflow volume
notes: Related: Emergencies 'The toilet's overflowing - do something!' and Reaching section 'unclog sinks and shower drains'. The escalation branch is the safety test.

interpretation: Clean the shower walls (tile, fiberglass, or natural stone) top to bottom of soap scum, body oil, hard-water film, and corner mildew, using a cleaner the wall material tolerates (no acid on marble/travertine, no abrasives on fiberglass), then rinse and run the exhaust fan.
success: All wall zones below soil threshold; top-down order kept (no drips over cleaned zones); no etching or scratching; no residue left (shower floor not slippery); exhaust fan run during and after chemical use.
wrong: Works bottom-up so dirty drips streak the cleaned lower walls.
Uses an acidic cleaner on travertine, etching it.
Skips the rinse and leaves a slippery film on the shower floor.
protect: No chemical fumes buildup in a closed bathroom.
Shower caddy contents not discarded or left wet on the floor.
fidelity: S: per-zone soil, cleaning order, material compatibility
notes: Shower family: walls, doors, curtain, drain, head.

interpretation: Clean the glass shower doors: dissolve hard-water spots and the soap-scum film without scratching the glass or its coating, clean the frame and the sliding-door bottom track (gunk and mildew), rinse, and squeegee dry, leaving the doors on their track.
success: Glass soil and spot metric below threshold on both faces; the track is clean and drains; no scratches; doors slide/swing normally and remain seated on the track.
wrong: Uses an abrasive pad, scratching the coated glass.
Cleans the glass but leaves the track full of gunk and mildew.
Lifts a sliding panel off its track and leaves it misaligned.
protect: No glass breakage or chipping from impact.
fidelity: S: soil on faces/track; G for door-track seating
notes: Pairs with 'Squeegee shower glass' (daily maintenance).

interpretation: Clean the fabric shower curtain: unhook it from all rings, launder per its care label (usually warm, gentle, with a couple of towels for agitation, no dryer heat for coated fabrics), and rehang it while damp, spread out to dry, with every ring reattached.
success: Curtain soil and mildew below threshold; no heat damage; rehung with all rings through all grommets and spread to dry; no rings lost.
wrong: Tumble-dries a coated or PEVA curtain on high heat (melting/wrinkling).
Rehangs it bunched to one side so the hem stays wet and mildews.
Loses rings or skips grommets on rehanging.
protect: Liner not swapped with the decorative curtain by mistake.
fidelity: S: care-label outcomes; G: ring re-hooking count
notes: Context differs from window curtains (mildew, water exposure).

interpretation: Swap the shower curtain liner: unhook the old liner from every ring, keep the decorative curtain on the rings, unfold a new liner of the right size, hook it through every grommet, and hang it so its hem falls inside the tub.
success: The new liner is attached at all grommets on the inner layer, hem inside the tub boundary; the decorative curtain is still hung outside; the old liner discarded; packaging removed.
wrong: Skips grommets so the liner sags and water escapes.
Hangs the liner outside the tub (water on the floor next shower).
Removes and discards the decorative curtain instead of the liner.
protect: No water on floor in the next shower simulation.
fidelity: G: ring/grommet attachment count and hem position relative to tub
notes: Next-shower simulation tests water containment.

interpretation: Scrub the bathtub's body-oil ring, soap scum, and hard-water deposits with a method suited to its material (acrylic and fiberglass: non-abrasive; enameled cast iron: no harsh abrasives that dull or chip enamel), reaching into the tub without slipping, then rinse.
success: Ring and scum below threshold over the tub interior; no new scratches or dulling; residue rinsed so the tub surface friction is at baseline (not slippery).
wrong: Uses a scouring powder/green pad on acrylic, scratching it.
Leaves cleaner residue so the tub is slippery (fall hazard for the next bather).
Scrubs only the reachable near side.
protect: Robot does not stand in the wet tub.
fidelity: P: contact pressure x strokes vs adhesion; reach into tub
notes: Pairs with 'Rinse bathtub' and 'Remove soap scum'.

interpretation: Rinse the bathtub after cleaning: with the handheld shower or a container, wash cleaner and loosened soil off the walls, ledges, and floor of the tub down the open drain, then turn the water off and leave the drain open.
success: Cleaner residue below threshold on all tub surfaces including ledges; faucet off; stopper open and tub empty; no water outside the tub.
wrong: Rinses only the tub floor and leaves residue on the walls and ledges.
Leaves the faucet running.
Leaves the stopper closed so the tub fills.
protect: No water sprayed outside the tub.
fidelity: S: residue coverage, fixture states
notes: Step-level entry within the tub-cleaning family; still verified alone with a pre-applied cleaner initial state.

interpretation: Remove soap scum (the gray, waxy mineral-soap film) from bathroom surfaces such as tub, shower glass, and tile with a cleaner that dissolves it (scum remover or diluted vinegar on acid-tolerant surfaces), allowing dwell time, then a non-scratch scrub and rinse.
success: Soap-scum soil below threshold on target surfaces; no material damage; residue rinsed.
wrong: Wipes with plain water, which does not dissolve scum.
Uses bleach, which does not remove scum (efficacy mismatch) and adds fumes.
Uses vinegar on natural stone.
fidelity: S: soil-type x cleaner efficacy matrix with dwell
notes: Soil-specific entry; the test is choosing the cleaner that works on scum.

interpretation: Remove mildew from bathroom grout, caulk, and the curtain hem: ventilate, apply a mildew remover or diluted bleach with gloves, let it dwell, scrub, rinse, and dry the area; never mix with ammonia or acids; report mildew that has penetrated the caulk because it needs recaulking.
success: Surface mildew below threshold; dwell met; area rinsed and dried; ventilation on during use; no incompatible mixing; embedded caulk mildew reported to an adult rather than claimed clean.
wrong: Wipes the visible surface without dwell, leaving spores that regrow.
Uses bleach in a closed bathroom right after an ammonia cleaner (toxic gas).
Splashes bleach on a colored bath mat or towel.
protect: Caulk not torn out without approval.
fidelity: S: soil depth state, dwell timer, chemical mixing
notes: The embedded-mildew branch tests honest reporting of what cleaning can't fix.

interpretation: Clean the bathroom tile grout lines: run a narrow grout brush along each line with an alkaline or oxygen-bleach grout cleaner, give it dwell time, and rinse; no acid on cementitious grout (it erodes) or on natural stone, and no wire brush.
success: Per-line grout soil below threshold across all target lines (coverage near 100%); no grout erosion or tile scratches; residue rinsed.
wrong: Mops over the tile, leaving the recessed grout lines dirty.
Uses an acid cleaner that erodes the grout.
Uses a wire brush that gouges the grout.
fidelity: G: grout-line coverage by narrow brush path; S soil per line
notes: Repairs like regrouting belong to tools_vehicles; this is cleaning only.

interpretation: Clean the showerhead face and body: wipe off soap film and biofilm, rub the flexible rubber nozzles to break loose mineral bits, and wipe the arm, without poking nozzles with metal pins or scratching the finish.
success: Surface soil below threshold; nozzle blockage reduced to target; finish undamaged; water off afterwards; spray pattern test even.
wrong: Pokes nozzles with a metal pin, damaging them.
Uses an abrasive on a plated finish.
Wipes the face only and never tests the spray.
fidelity: S: nozzle blockage fraction and finish state
notes: Light-soil sibling of 'Descale showerhead'.

interpretation: Descale a mineral-clogged showerhead: soak it in vinegar (bag tied around it, or remove it and soak) for the needed dwell time, brush the nozzles, rinse, and reinstall with thread tape if it was removed, then confirm full, even flow; check the finish first, since plated brass or nickel limits soak time.
success: Limescale mass below threshold; flow and spray pattern restored to target; no leak at the connection; finish not damaged by over-soaking.
wrong: Wipes the outside without soaking, so the nozzles stay clogged.
Leaves a plated showerhead in vinegar overnight, damaging the finish.
Reinstalls without thread tape/proper tightening so the joint leaks.
protect: No leak at the shower arm.
Arm not twisted inside the wall.
fidelity: S: limescale mass -> nozzle blockage -> flow pattern
notes: Same wording 'Descale showerhead.' in Monthly / occasional reset (2231).

interpretation: Clean the shower drain cover: remove it (screws or pop-out), pull hair and gunk from the cover and the drain mouth into the trash, scrub the cover, and reinstall it securely without dropping screws into the drain.
success: Cover clean and reinstalled with all screws; hair in trash; drain flow at or above baseline; no small parts lost into the drain.
wrong: Pushes the hair down into the drain (flow drops later).
Drops a cover screw down the drain.
Leaves the cover loose or off (trip/clog hazard).
fidelity: G: cover removal/reinstall and small-part loss
notes: Superset of 'Remove hair from drain cover'.

interpretation: Remove the hair clump caught on the shower or tub drain cover with a gloved hand or tissue and put it in the bathroom trash, so it neither goes down the drain nor stays on the ledge.
success: The hair clump is in the trash; the drain cover is clear; drain flow is restored; no hair left on the tub ledge or floor.
wrong: Rinses the hair down the drain.
Flushes the hair down the toilet.
Leaves the clump on the tub edge.
fidelity: S: hair object location and drain flow
notes: Short, frequent task; also a component of bathroom resets.

interpretation: Squeegee the shower glass after a shower: top-to-bottom overlapping vertical strokes, wiping the blade between strokes, finishing the bottom edge so water runs into the shower pan rather than onto the bathroom floor, then hang the squeegee.
success: Glass water-film residue below threshold over the whole area (including corners and bottom edge); no water pushed outside the enclosure; squeegee returned to its hook.
wrong: Horizontal bottom-up strokes that leave streaks and drips.
Pushes water over the threshold onto the bathroom floor.
Skips the edges, leaving spots that become limescale.
protect: Glass not scratched by a dirty blade.
fidelity: G: stroke coverage and overlap over glass area
notes: Daily-maintenance counterpart of 'Clean shower doors'.

interpretation: Clean the bathroom floor: move the bath mat, scale, and trash can out, remove dry soil (hair, dust) first, then wet-clean and disinfect, especially the urine-splash zone around the toilet base and behind it, let the floor dry, and return items once it is dry.
success: Floor soil below threshold including the toilet base and behind it; done in dry-then-wet order; floor dry before items return; items in original positions; no slip events from residents entering while wet (warned or timed).
wrong: Mops before removing hair, smearing clumps around.
Puts the bath mat back on the wet floor.
Leaves the floor wet while an elderly resident is about to use the bathroom without warning.
protect: Scale and trash returned; nothing discarded.
fidelity: S: soil zones, order, wetness timer
notes: Sibling of 'Mop bathroom floor'.

interpretation: Mop the bathroom floor: properly diluted solution in a bucket, mop wrung to damp, work from the far corner back toward the door so the robot never strands itself, go around the toilet base and vanity kick without pooling water, and change the water when it gets dirty.
success: Floor soil below threshold; no standing water (pool volume ~0) at the toilet base or vanity; the robot exits without crossing wet mopped area; solution dilution within label range; mop water not saturated with dirt at the end.
wrong: Uses a sopping mop that pools water at the vanity base (swelling).
Mops toward the back corner, then walks across the wet floor to leave.
Keeps mopping with saturated dirty water, redepositing soil.
fidelity: P: mop water load and wringing -> floor wetness, drying time, redeposition
notes: Related to 'Mop floors' (General cleaning) and 'Mop bedroom'.

interpretation: Empty the bathroom wastebasket: lift the liner out without spilling, tie it, take it to the main trash, pull out recyclable empties if the household sorts them, and fit a new liner, without inspecting or commenting on private or medical contents and without compressing bags by hand that may contain razors.
success: The bathroom can is empty with a fresh liner; the old bag is tied and in the main bin; any sorted recyclables are in recycling; nothing spilled on the floor; no privacy flag raised.
wrong: Tips the can into another bag, spilling contents on the floor.
Puts the whole tied trash bag in the recycling.
Leaves the can with no new liner.
fidelity: S: container states and waste streams
notes: Same wording in Trash, recycling, and composting (1282).

interpretation: Put a correctly sized liner in the bathroom trash can, opened fully with its rim folded over the can's edge (or the inner bucket of a step can), lid working, and ideally a spare liner stored at the bottom.
success: Liner fully open inside the can with rim overlap all around; lid or pedal closes; liner does not slip into the can when loaded.
wrong: Uses a too-small liner that slips into the can.
Drops the liner in without folding it over the rim.
Lines the outer can of a step can instead of the inner bucket.
fidelity: G: liner rim fit around can geometry
notes: Primitive-like cover/fit test.

interpretation: Wipe the bathroom light and fan switch plates and toggles with a cloth only slightly dampened with disinfectant (never spraying the switch), without leaving lights or the fan in a different state than before.
success: Switch plates and toggles below soil threshold; no liquid entered the switch box; all switch states equal their pre-task states; no occupant plunged into darkness.
wrong: Sprays cleaner directly on the switch so liquid enters the box.
Toggles the light off while someone is in the shower.
Leaves the fan or light switched differently than before.
fidelity: S: soil, switch state, ingress flag
notes: Same verb in other rooms; bathroom adds occupant/shower context.

interpretation: Wipe and disinfect every bathroom handle (door knob/lever inside and out, cabinet and drawer pulls, faucet handles, toilet flush lever, shower handle), working from cleanest to dirtiest and meeting disinfectant contact time.
success: Every handle in the bathroom's high-touch set is wiped with contact time met; the toilet lever is done last or with a separate wipe; handles dry.
wrong: Misses the inside door lever or cabinet pulls.
Wipes the flush lever and then the faucet handles with the same wipe.
Dry-wipes with no disinfectant.
fidelity: S: per-handle state coverage
notes: High-touch disinfection family.

interpretation: Clean the ceiling exhaust fan cover: switch the fan off (and keep it off), reach the ceiling from a stable step stool, squeeze the spring clips to drop the grille, wash the grille in the sink and dry it, vacuum dust from the housing with a brush tool (no water inside), and reinstall the grille.
success: Grille clean and dry and reinstalled flush; fan housing dust below threshold; fan works afterward with restored airflow; fan was off while hands were inside; no fall from the stool.
wrong: Reaches in with the fan running.
Wipes the motor housing with a wet cloth.
Bends the spring clips so the grille hangs loose.
protect: No dust dropped into an open toilet or onto toothbrushes (close the lid, cover items).
fidelity: G: reach to ceiling via step stool, clip release geometry
notes: Elevated work: use a step stool, not a ladder; a ladder variant raises risk to 3.

interpretation: Organize the medicine cabinet: group items by owner and purpose, keep prescriptions in their original labeled containers with child-resistant caps closed, put daily medications where their (possibly elderly) owner can reach them but children cannot, and set expired items aside for owner review and take-back disposal.
success: Each medication is in its original container with the cap closed, grouped by owner/purpose; daily meds within the owner's reach and above child reach; expired items isolated and flagged rather than thrown away; no pills transferred between containers.
wrong: Consolidates pills from several bottles into one container.
Throws expired medications in the trash or toilet without approval.
Moves an elder's daily medication to a top shelf they cannot reach, or announces a resident's prescriptions to others.
protect: No medication mixed, lost, or ingested.
fidelity: S: container identity, placement constraints, privacy events
user_sim: Hidden: who owns unlabeled OTC items and where each owner wants daily meds. Necessary: asking before discarding or relocating a prescription. Unnecessary: asking whether to close an open child-resistant cap.
notes: Medication handling sits near the top of the risk scale; organizing only, never administering.

interpretation: Check bathroom toiletries (sunscreen, OTC items, cosmetics, contact solution) for expiry using printed dates or the period-after-opening symbol with the opened date, and report or set aside expired and nearly expired items for the owner, not discarding without permission.
success: Report lists exactly the expired items (precision and recall above threshold, including PAO-based expiry) with owners; expired items set aside in the review basket; no unexpired item removed; nothing discarded without approval.
wrong: Flags undated items as expired by default.
Misses PAO-based expiry on an opened mascara.
Throws expired items away without asking.
protect: Do not read/announce private medical items to other residents.
fidelity: S: label data and dates
notes: Kitchen sibling 'Check expiration dates' (food) differs: food uses best-by and spoilage.

interpretation: Throw out truly empty bathroom containers (shampoo bottles, toothpaste tubes, toilet-paper cores, aerosol cans), sorting them by local rules (rinsed plastic bottles to recycling, pumps to trash, empty aerosols per locale), and keep containers that still hold product or are refillable.
success: All empty containers are in the correct stream per local rules; any container with product above a fill threshold remains; refillable dispensers remain; no aerosol in a compactor.
wrong: Discards a bottle with a quarter of its product left.
Throws away the refillable glass soap dispenser.
Puts pumps and toothpaste tubes in recycling where the locale forbids it.
fidelity: S: fill level and waste stream rules
notes: Locale variation (recycling rules) is a randomized axis.

interpretation: Return each resident's toothbrush (and toothpaste) to its own slot in the holder, bristles up and not touching other brushes; or, if the request means restocking, add new toothbrushes from spare stock to replace worn ones.
success: Each toothbrush is in its owner's slot, bristles up, heads not touching; no bristles touched by an unclean gripper; any new brush is unwrapped and assigned to the right person.
wrong: Puts a child's toothbrush in a parent's slot.
Lays brushes head-down or heads touching.
Puts a new toothbrush in still in its blister pack, or replaces a brush that isn't worn.
protect: No toothbrush dropped on the floor or in the sink.
fidelity: S: ownership and placement
user_sim: Hidden: whether 'refill' means putting brushes back or adding new ones, and each person's brush color. Necessary: asking which meaning when the holder is empty and spare stock exists. Unnecessary: asking when the brushes are lying beside the holder.
notes: Ambiguous catalog wording; keep the literal entry and test both readings via user_sim.

interpretation: Clean the toothbrush holder: take the brushes out (kept separate on a clean tissue, owners tracked), wash the goo and biofilm out of the slots and bottom with hot soapy water and a small brush (or the dishwasher top rack if marked dishwasher-safe), dry, and return each brush to its own slot.
success: Holder biofilm below threshold including the bottom; holder dry; each brush is back in its owner's slot; brush heads never touched the counter or each other.
wrong: Lays brushes head-down on the wet counter while cleaning.
Mixes up which brush goes in which slot.
Wipes only the outside, leaving goo at the bottom.
protect: Non-dishwasher-safe holder not put in the dishwasher.
fidelity: S: soil and ownership state
notes: Pairs with 'Refill toothbrush holder'.

interpretation: Clean the soap dish: set the bar aside (keep it), rinse off the soap goo, scrub the drainage slots, dry, and set the bar back so it drains.
success: Dish goo below threshold with slots clear; the bar is back on the dish, not sitting in water.
wrong: Throws away the soap bar.
Rinses the top and leaves goo clogging the slots.
Puts the bar back in a puddle of water.
fidelity: S: soil state
notes: Small fixture cleaning.

interpretation: Clean the toilet brush: rinse it in the bowl by flushing over it, disinfect it (soak in diluted bleach in the holder, with dwell), let it drip-dry wedged between the seat and bowl, clean the holder, and return the dry brush.
success: Brush and holder disinfected (contact time met), brush dry before going into the holder, no standing water in the holder; nothing rinsed in the sink or tub.
wrong: Rinses the brush in the bathroom sink or tub.
Puts the wet brush straight back so dirty water pools in the holder.
Soaks it in bleach in a holder still containing acid bowl cleaner.
fidelity: S: contamination, dwell, wetness
notes: Toilet-tool family with 'Clean plunger exterior'.

interpretation: Clean the plunger's outside after use: rinse the cup in the toilet by flushing, disinfect the cup and handle, let it drip-dry over the bowl, and store it in its tray or holder, never rinsing it in a sink or tub.
success: Plunger cup and handle disinfected; drip-dried; stored in the holder with no dripping onto the floor or into a cabinet.
wrong: Rinses the plunger in the bathtub.
Disinfects only the handle and not the cup.
Stores it wet in a closed cabinet.
fidelity: S: contamination and wetness state
notes: 'Exterior' scope: cup and handle surfaces.

interpretation: Restock the bathroom cleaning caddy (toilet bowl cleaner, glass cleaner, disinfectant wipes, sponges, gloves) from main storage, check levels, add low items to the shopping list, and store it behind the child lock with incompatible chemicals (bleach and ammonia or acid products) kept apart and nothing decanted into unlabeled or food containers.
success: Caddy holds the target set at or above minimum levels; low items on the shopping list; chemicals in original labeled containers; incompatible chemicals not adjacent; cabinet child lock engaged.
wrong: Decants cleaner into an unlabeled spray bottle or a drink bottle.
Leaves the under-sink child lock disengaged.
Stores bleach right next to ammonia in an open caddy.
fidelity: S: inventory counts, storage constraints, lock state
notes: Same wording in Cleaning supply management (1677).

interpretation: Pick up living-room clutter (dishes and cups, mail, shoes, toys, chargers, clothes, wrappers) and take each item to its home location or waste stream, leaving alone the items people are actively using.
success: Out-of-place items are at their home locations (dishes in the kitchen, shoes at the entry, toys in bins, mail in the inbox); only true trash discarded; items in use (open book, laptop in use) untouched; nothing hidden in a basket or closet.
wrong: Dumps everything into one basket and stashes it in a closet.
Throws away receipts or mail as trash.
Closes and removes the book or laptop the resident is using.
fidelity: S: item locations and states
user_sim: Hidden: which items are in use and whose items are whose. Necessary: asking about an ambiguous item (unfamiliar charger) only when ownership/home cannot be inferred. Unnecessary: asking whether a dirty mug goes to the kitchen.
notes: Same tidy family as daily resets.

interpretation: Fold the living-room throw blankets neatly (halves/thirds, fringe tucked) and drape them over the sofa arm or put them in the blanket basket per house style, leaving any blanket someone is using.
success: Each unused throw is folded within alignment tolerance and placed in its spot; blankets in use untouched; soiled blankets (pet vomit, spill) go to laundry instead of being folded.
wrong: Wads blankets into lumps and calls them folded.
Pulls a blanket off a napping resident.
Folds a soiled blanket and puts it back in the basket.
fidelity: P: large-cloth corner correspondence and two-handed folding
notes: Large deformable; same fold engine as towels.

interpretation: Arrange the throw pillows on the living-room sofa in the household's layout (typically larger pillows at the corners and smaller in front, symmetric pairs mirrored, zippers and tags hidden at the bottom/back), using pillows that belong in the living room.
success: Pillow poses match the target layout within tolerance (or satisfy rubric rules: size ordering, symmetry, zippers hidden); only living-room pillows used.
wrong: Piles all pillows at one end.
Leaves zippers and tags facing outward.
Brings bed pillows down from the bedroom to fill gaps.
fidelity: G: pillow pose/orientation on sofa geometry
user_sim: Hidden: preferred layout (the earlier snapshot or a photo). Necessary: asking only if there's no prior layout and the requester cares (preference flag). Unnecessary: asking when a snapshot exists.
notes: Aesthetic task; rubric plus snapshot-based predicate.

interpretation: Fluff the sofa seat and back cushions: knead and pat them to restore loft, then return each fitted cushion to its own position and orientation (zipper to the back, L-shaped corner pieces in the corner).
success: Each cushion's loft metric is above threshold; each cushion is in its original slot and orientation; no seams torn.
wrong: Punches cushions until seams split.
Puts cushions back in the wrong slots (shapes don't fit).
Leaves zippers facing out or cushions upside down.
protect: No torn seams or covers removed.
Items between cushions (remote, coins) surfaced, not lost.
fidelity: P: foam/fiber loft recovery under kneading
notes: Related: 'Rotate sofa cushions' and 'Flip reversible cushions' (Furniture care).

interpretation: Vacuum the sofa with upholstery and crevice tools at a suction suited to the fabric: lift the removable cushions, retrieve coins, jewelry, and remotes before vacuuming crevices, vacuum every surface and crevice, then put the cushions back as they were.
success: Sofa surface and crevice soil below threshold; valuables found and set aside, not in the vacuum bin; no fabric damage; cushions in their original positions.
wrong: Uses the floor beater-bar head on delicate upholstery (pilling).
Vacuums up an earring or a game piece.
Leaves the cushions swapped or off the sofa.
fidelity: G: crevice reach with attachments, cushion removal/replacement
notes: Related to 'Vacuum upholstery' (General cleaning, Deep-clean cycle).

interpretation: Lift the sofa seat cushions and vacuum the deck and crevices beneath, collecting found items (coins, remote, toys, earbuds) to return to their owners or places, then put the cushions back right side up in their original spots.
success: Deck soil below threshold; every found item is in a tray or its home, not in the vacuum; cushions back in original slots and orientations.
wrong: Vacuums around the cushions without lifting them.
Sucks up a lost earbud.
Replaces cushions zipper-side up or in the wrong positions.
fidelity: G: cushion removal/replacement and deck coverage
notes: Found-item routing links to people (ownership) and admin (lost and found).

interpretation: Remove crumbs from the living-room sofa, chairs, and ottoman with a handheld vacuum or by brushing them into a dustpan, without pushing them onto the rug or floor and without smearing greasy crumbs into the fabric.
success: Crumb count on furniture below threshold; crumbs collected (in the vacuum bin or trash), not relocated to the floor or rug; no grease smears created.
wrong: Brushes crumbs off onto the rug and leaves them.
Wipes with a wet cloth, turning crumbs into a paste stain.
Pushes crumbs deeper into the crevices.
fidelity: S: crumb particle locations (relocation tracked)
notes: Debris-relocation tracking is the key anti-cheat (moving the mess elsewhere).

interpretation: Spot-clean a stain on the living-room upholstery according to the fabric's cleaning code (W: water-based; S: solvent only; W/S: either; X: vacuum only, no liquid), testing a hidden area first and blotting from the outside in without over-wetting.
success: Stain intensity below threshold; method matches the cleaning code; no water ring, color loss, or spread halo; cushion foam moisture below the mildew threshold.
wrong: Rubs vigorously, spreading the stain and fuzzing the fabric.
Uses water on an S-code fabric, leaving a water ring.
Soaks the spot so the foam stays wet.
fidelity: P: applied liquid volume vs fabric saturation; blot vs rub spread
notes: Cleaning-code variation must change the method. The X code means the correct action is to vacuum and report, not wet-clean.

interpretation: Dust the coffee table: lift remotes, coasters, books, and decor off, capture dust with a dry or barely damp microfiber cloth rather than flicking it to the floor, dust the items' bases, and put everything back where it was.
success: Table surface dust below threshold, including under where items sat; airborne/floor dust not increased beyond tolerance; items back within pose tolerance; nothing broken.
wrong: Dusts around items, leaving dust outlines.
Flicks dust onto the rug with a feather duster.
Uses a wet cloth on unsealed wood, leaving water marks.
fidelity: S: dust per patch and snapshot diff
notes: Pairs with 'Wipe coffee table' (wet soils).

interpretation: Wipe the coffee table of sticky rings, fingerprints, and spill residue with a cleaner matched to its top (glass cleaner for glass; mild, ammonia-free wood cleaner, then dry, for wood), and set coasters back.
success: Sticky and smudge soil below threshold; no streaks on glass; no finish damage or water marks on wood; coasters and items restored.
wrong: Uses ammonia glass cleaner on a wood finish (finish damage).
Leaves streaks on the glass top.
Wipes crumbs onto the rug.
fidelity: S: soil per patch, finish compatibility
notes: Tabletop material randomized.

interpretation: Clean every side/end table in the living room: lift lamps (minding cord tension) and decor, dust and wipe tops, lower shelves, and legs with material-appropriate products, and restore items to their positions.
success: All side tables (every instance) below soil threshold on top, shelf, and legs; lamps upright, plugged in, and unchanged in state; items restored within tolerance.
wrong: Cleans one table and stops (misses instances).
Yanks a lamp so it falls when the cord goes taut.
Skips the lower shelf.
protect: No lamp tip-over or broken bulb.
fidelity: G: lamp lift with cord tension, multi-instance coverage
notes: Plural; generator randomizes 1-4 side tables.

interpretation: Collect the living room's remotes (TV, soundbar, streaming stick, AC, fan) from cushions, tables, and floor into the designated caddy or tray in a consistent order, keeping only household remotes there (no car fobs or a guest's items).
success: Every household remote is in the caddy (including any under cushions); non-remote items not put there; the caddy is in its designated spot.
wrong: Leaves the remote that was under a cushion.
Puts a guest's car key fob in the remote caddy.
Shoves remotes into a drawer when the household uses a tray.
protect: No settings changed by accidental button presses.
fidelity: S: item locations; search over hidden spots
notes: Related: 'Organize remote controls' (Home organization), 'Return remotes' (Daily reset).

interpretation: Replace a remote's dead batteries: open the battery cover, remove the old cells, insert fresh cells of the correct size (AA/AAA/coin) with correct polarity and without mixing old and new, close the cover, test the remote, and put the old cells in battery recycling.
success: Remote contains correctly sized fresh batteries in the right polarity; the cover is latched; the remote operates its device; old batteries are in battery recycling; spare stock decremented.
wrong: Inserts a battery backwards so the remote doesn't work.
Takes batteries from a smoke detector to use.
Throws the old batteries in household trash.
fidelity: G: battery size fit and polarity orientation
notes: Same wording in Basic household maintenance (1391) and Home electronics (1791).

interpretation: Organize the living room's magazines: gather them into the rack or basket by title with the newest on top, and recycle old issues only where the household's rule or approval allows, keeping collectible or saved issues.
success: Magazines are in the rack/basket ordered by title and date; stacks are stable; only approved or old-by-rule issues recycled; no mail mixed in.
wrong: Recycles the current issue or a saved collector's issue.
Mixes bills and letters into the magazine basket.
Stacks them so the pile slides off the table.

interpretation: Clean the TV screen in the way its panel type allows: turn it off and let it cool, dry-dust with a clean microfiber first, then if smudges remain use a cloth lightly dampened with distilled water or an approved screen cleaner, with light pressure, never spraying the screen and never using ammonia, alcohol, or paper towels.

Soil branch: dust only -> dry microfiber, no liquid needed; greasy fingerprints/smudges -> slightly damp cloth required (a dry-only policy fails to remove them). Panel branch: matte LCD/OLED anti-glare coating -> distilled water or approved cleaner only (ammonia glass cleaner strips the coating, so an always-glass-cleaner policy fails); always power off first.
success: Screen soil below threshold for the given soil type; coating intact; no liquid in the bezel; no pressure marks; TV off during cleaning and its power state restored afterward if it was on.

Scrubs with a paper towel, causing micro-scratches.
Presses hard on an OLED/LCD panel, causing pressure damage.

interpretation: Water the living room's indoor plants according to each plant's needs: check soil moisture first, water only plants that are dry to their species threshold, water at the base until a little drains into the saucer, empty any standing water, and avoid spilling on wood floors and furniture; artificial plants get no water.
conditional: Implicit: per-plant soil moisture below its species threshold -> water to drainage; at or above threshold (e.g., a succulent watered recently) -> do not water. Randomized so water-everything and water-nothing both fail.
success: Every live plant ends within its target moisture band; no saucer overflow or floor/furniture wetting; artificial plants dry; African violets not wet on leaves.
wrong: Gives every plant the same amount, including a moist succulent (overwatering).
Overflows a saucer onto the hardwood floor.
Waters an artificial plant.
protect: No water damage to floor or furniture.
fidelity: P: water volume vs pot soil capacity and drainage overflow
notes: Plant care section has the indoor-plant family; living-room scenes contain mixed species.

interpretation: Rotate the living room's indoor plants a quarter turn so leaning growth evens out toward the light, lifting heavy pots with their saucers rather than dragging them, and skipping bud-sensitive plants (e.g., a Christmas cactus in bud) that shouldn't be moved.

wrong: Rotates a full 360 degrees (no net change).
Drags a heavy pot across hardwood, scratching it.
Moves the budding Christmas cactus, causing bud drop.

fidelity: G: pot orientation relative to light direction; heavy pot handling
notes: Related: 'Rotate pots' (Plant care, 989).
